documents.summary: Teaching-center guidance that explains why blanket AI bans are hard to enforce and may hinder skills, then offers four sample syllabus statements from open use to restriction. It leaves the stance to each instructor and recommends discussing it on day one.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no single rule: it says 'AI syllabus policies should be being clear, flexible, learner-centered and process-focused' and offers four sample statements ranging from 'encourages and embraces' to 'not to be used ... unless specifically directed', so the decision is left to instructors.

documents.title: MOA 2514 revision: syllabus AI requirements
documents.summary: A Faculty Senate memorandum, signed March 2026, that adds a required AI statement to the list of syllabus elements. It requires instructors to state their AI expectations explicitly and treats unauthorized or undisclosed AI use as an academic integrity violation under the Student Code.
documents.stance_why: The memorandum says it will 'require faculty to explicitly state how AI can and cannot be used in the classroom without dictating what that looks like for faculty', so it sets no stance and hands the decision to instructors.
